Queue operators¶

Back to Queue API Reference

Signature¶

Queue operator+() const;
Queue operator-() const;

Queue operator+(const Queue& rhs) const;
Queue operator-(const Queue& rhs) const;
Queue operator*(const Queue& rhs) const;
Queue operator/(const Queue& rhs) const;
Queue operator%(const Queue& rhs) const;

Queue operator==(const Queue& rhs) const;
Queue operator!=(const Queue& rhs) const;
Queue operator<(const Queue& rhs) const;
Queue operator<=(const Queue& rhs) const;
Queue operator>(const Queue& rhs) const;
Queue operator>=(const Queue& rhs) const;

What It Does¶

Unary + is a no-op – it returns *this unchanged, for every kind. Unary - calls invoke("neg"), which only Series and Duration support; calling it on a Note- or Timeline-holding Queue throws.

The binary arithmetic and comparison operators first check that both sides have the same kind() – a mismatch throws before anything else happens. With matching kinds, Series, Timeline, and Duration payloads route straight through invoke with the matching operation name ("add", "sub", "mul", "div", "mod", "eq", "ne", "lt", "le", "gt", "ge"). Note payloads are the exception: only + is supported (text concatenation, via Note’s own operator+), and all six comparisons are supported too (each wrapped so the result comes back as a proper boolean Series rather than Note’s own byte-mask representation) – but -, *, /, and % all throw for Note payloads, since none of them are meaningful operations on text.

Parameters¶

rhs (const Queue&)

The right-hand operand. Must have the same kind() as the left-hand side.

Returns¶

A new Queue, with the arithmetic operators returning the same kind as both operands and the comparison operators returning a Series-holding Queue of booleans in every case (including when both operands are Note).

Errors¶

Throws when the two operands have different kinds, or when the operation isn’t supported for the operands’ shared kind (any of -, *, /, % on Note; unary - on Note or Timeline).

Examples¶

Example 1. Unary +/- and the binary arithmetic and comparison operators on two Series-holding Queues.

pluss::Queue a(pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0}));
pluss::Queue b(pluss::make_series({10.0, 20.0, 30.0}));
std::cout << "+a (unary, no-op): " << pluss::series::print((+a).series()) << '\n';
std::cout << "-a (unary neg): " << pluss::series::print((-a).series()) << '\n';
std::cout << "a + b: " << pluss::series::print((a + b).series()) << '\n';
std::cout << "a * b: " << pluss::series::print((a * b).series()) << '\n';
std::cout << "a < b: " << pluss::series::print((a < b).series()) << '\n';
std::cout << "a == a: " << pluss::series::print((a == a).series()) << '\n';

Output¶

+a (unary, no-op): Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[1.0000, 2.0000, 3.0000]
-a (unary neg): Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[-1.0000, -2.0000, -3.0000]
a + b: Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[11.0000, 22.0000, 33.0000]
a * b: Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[10.0000, 40.0000, 90.0000]
a < b: Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[true, true, true]
a == a: Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[true, true, true]

Example 2. Note payloads: + concatenates text and succeeds; * is not a meaningful text operation and throws.

pluss::Queue note_a(pluss::make_note({"x"}));
pluss::Queue note_b(pluss::make_note({"y"}));
pluss::Queue note_sum = note_a + note_b;
std::cout << "note + note: " << note_sum.note() << '\n';
try {
  pluss::Queue bad = note_a * note_b;
  std::cout << "note * note: did not throw\n";
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string msg = e.what();
  std::cout << "note * note threw: " << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << '\n';
}

Output¶

note + note: Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["xy"]
note * note threw: Queue::operator* failed: Queue::operator*: unsupported for Note payloads

"x" + "y" concatenates to "xy", the same as calling Note’s own operator+ directly.
